step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified visual external actors on the left side of the whiteboard: 'CLI' (developers deploying code, mapped to UserCompanyDeveloper) and 'Browser' (end-users invoking applications, mapped to UserConsumerWeb).
2. Identified AWS services drawn as individual nodes on the whiteboard:
   - Top-left EC2: Web service handling CLI deployment requests.
   - Top DynamoDB: Stores deployment progress/state.
   - Middle SQS: Queue decoupling deployment requests.
   - Top-right EC2: Backend service processing SQS messages and deploying Lambda functions.
   - Bottom-middle EC2: Internal service processing browser requests, checking permissions, and invoking Lambdas.
   - Right Lambda: Customer code execution running in a separate AWS account (divided by green line).
3. Traced all physical directed arrows to establish data flows:
   - Flow 0 (Deployment path): CLI -> EC2 -> DynamoDB & SQS -> EC2 -> Lambda.
   - Flow 1 (Invocation path): Browser -> EC2 -> Lambda.

graph.name: Atlassian Forge Platform Architecture
graph.notes: The architecture separates the core Atlassian Forge platform account from customer Lambda execution accounts using account boundaries and V8 isolates for tenant isolation.
